conflict_resolutions.PARTIAL_OR_QUALIFIED_CHANGE_REQUIRES_CLA: The OFR note 'Superseded by: EO 8384 (in part)' is only a qualifier on an editorial line. I read EO 8384 sec. 21 in full: it supersedes EO 7845 by number with no exception for any section of EO 7845; the only proviso concerns the total leave credited when sections 6 and 9 of EO 8384 apply retroactively to July 1, 1936. The partial-change flag is therefore resolved against a partial reading.

notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 7845 (3 FR 715, Mar. 21, 1938, No. 7845): Parts I-IV, secs. 1-22, regulations on annual leave of civilian officers and employees; it has no own term or sunset (the machine TERM leads are ordinary conditions such as the one-year accrual rule, not endings) and sec. 21 only supersedes EO 7409. I read the held full text of EO 8384 (5 FR 1253, Apr. 2, 1940, signed Mar. 29, 1940, [No. 8384]), a complete replacement set of annual-leave regulations. Part IV sec. 20 ratifies earlier departmental regulations and revokes inconsistent ones; sec. 21 states: 'This order shall supersede Executive Orders No. 7845 of March 21, 1938, No. 7879 of May 9, 1938, and No. 8226 of August 24, 1939, and shall be effective as of March 2, 1940, except that sections 6 and 9 shall be effective as of July 1, 1936, provided that the total amount of leave to the credit of any employee ... shall not exceed the amount authorized to be accumulated by law.' That names EO 7845 by number and ends the whole order; the proviso limits EO 8384's own retroactive sections and is not a savings clause for EO 7845. D6 self-check: the later events in the history are EO 7879/7880 (May 9, 1938, amending sec. 6), EO 8226 (Aug. 24, 1939, amending sec. 15) and EO 8384 itself; 7879/7880/8226 pre-date the basis and are themselves superseded in the same sec. 21, so none extends or revives 7845. The machine ACT:EO:7845>EO:8385 record is a false lead: EO 8385 is the companion sick-leave order and the held page extract only carries EO 8384's sec. 21 text; I do not cite it. No later held instrument mentions EO 7845 (a scan of the held full-run texts finds the number only in 7879, 7880, 8226, 8384, 8385 and the neighbouring page extracts of 8225/8227). The catalog line 'Supersedes: EO 7409; EO 8226' is a lead I do not rely on (EO 8226 amends 7845). No own term ran out earlier. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (Mar. 2, 1940 per sec. 21) is not otherwise adjudicated.
